'''Centum Electronics Limited''' is an Indian [[electronics]] system design and manufacturing company. The company produces [[subsystems]] and [[microelectronics]], and provides [[system integration]] services.<ref name="Forbes">{{Cite web|title=Centum Electronics|url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/centum-electronics/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref> The company was incorporated in January 1993 and is headquartered in [[Bengaluru]], [[Karnataka]]. Centum has a presence in 6 countries. It has manufacturing facilities, design, and sales and support teams in India, Canada, and France, a design team in Belgium, and sales and support teams in the United Kingdom and the United States.<ref>{{cite web |title=Investor Presentation September 2020 |url=http://www.valoremadvisors.com/pdf/centum-investor-presentation-2020.pdf |website=Valorem Advisors |access-date=26 January 2022 |date=September 2020}}</ref> The company's British subsidiary, Centum Electronics UK Ltd., services all European customers except those in [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-08-23|title=Centum investing Rs 200 cr in B'luru|url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/566353/centum-investing-rs-200-cr.html|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Deccan Herald|language=en}}</ref>  

Centum Electronics has multiple manufacturing facilities in Bangalore. The company opened its fourth Indian manufacturing facility at the Aerospace Park in [[Devanahalli]], near Bangalore on 15 February 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2017-02-16 |title=Centum Electronics opens fourth manufacturing facility in Bengaluru |url=https://www.business-standard.com/content/b2b-manufacturing-industry/centum-electronics-opens-fourth-manufacturing-facility-in-bengaluru-117021600370_1.html |access-date=2022-01-26 |work=Business Standard India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Dutta|first=Baishakhi|date=2017-02-21|title=Centum inaugurates new facility at Devanahalli Aerospace Park, Bangalore|url=https://www.electronicsb2b.com/industry-buzz/centum-inaugurates-new-facility-devanahalli-aerospace-park-bangalore/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=ElectronicsB2B|language=en-US}}</ref> Centum is one of the largest contractors to the [[ISRO|Indian Space Research Organisation]] (ISRO) and supplies over 50 different varieties of components for [[Satellite|satellites]] and [[Launch vehicle|launch vehicles]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The celestial bond that connects ISRO with India Inc|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/science/the-celestial-bond-that-connects-isro-with-india-inc/centum-for-micro-electronics/slideshow/70224320.cms|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Economic Times}}</ref> Centum opened a new space facility in [[Yelahanka]], Bangalore to support ISRO missions in September 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bureau&|first=Our|title=To meet ISROs growing number of missions, Centum Electronics opens new facility|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/national/to-meet-isros-growing-number-of-missions-centum-electronics-opens-new-facility/article29501964.ece|access-date=2022-01-26|website=thehindubusinessline.com|date=24 == History ==
[[Solectron]] Centum Electronics was founded on 8 January 1993 in Bangalore, Karnataka by Apparao Venkata Mallavarapu.<ref name="Forbes"/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Centum Electronics History {{!}} Centum Electronics Information|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/centum-electronics-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-8584.cms|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Economic Times|language=en}}</ref> The company was publicly listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and the [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Investor Relations – Centum|url=https://www.centumelectronics.com/investor-relations/|access-date=2022-01-26|language=en-US}}</ref> Centum Electronics demerged its [[electronics manufacturing services]] division into Solectron EMS India Ltd in November 2006.<ref>{{Cite news|title=OT-IT Convergence: Driving the Future of Industry 4.0 & Industry 5.0|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/engineering/ot-it-convergence-driving-the-future-of-industry-4-0-industry-5-0/articleshow/89093970.cms?from=mdr|access-date=2022-01-26}}</ref> The company changed its name to Centum Electronics in January 2013.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Reporter|first=B. S.|date=2007-12-14|title=Solectron Centum is now Centum Electronics|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/solectron-centum-is-now-centum-electronics-107121400018_1.html|access-date=2022-01-26}}</ref>

Centum acquired a 51% controlling stake in French company Adetel Group for an undisclosed amount in June 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-06-17|title=Centum Electronics picks 51% stake in French firm Adetel|url=https://www.vccircle.com/centum-electronics-picks-51-stake-french-firm-adetel|access-date=2022-01-26|website=VCCircle|language=en-US}}</ref> In April 2018, Centum signed an agreement to sell its 51% stake in Centum Rakon India Pvt. Ltd., a joint venture with New Zealand company [[Rakon]], to Rakon for US$5.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rakon confirms buyout of Centum Rakon India|url=https://www.rakon.com/news/rakon-confirms-buyout-of-centum-rakon-india|access-date=2022-01-26|website=www.rakon.com|language=en}}</ref> Centum stated that it did not regard Centum Rakon, which primarily operated in the telecommunications industry, as "core to its strategy".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-04-30|title=New Zealand electronics firm Rakon to buy out Bengaluru's Centum in JV|url=https://www.vccircle.com/new-zealand-electronics-firm-rakon-to-buy-out-bengalurus-centum-in-telecom-jv|access-date=2022-01-26|website=VCCircle|language=en-US}}</ref> The company increased its stake in Adetel Group to 64.66% in December 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Market|first=Capital|date=2020-12-11|title=Board of Centum Electronics approves further investment in Centum Adetel Group SA|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/board-of-centum-electronics-approves-further-investment-in-centum-adetel-group-sa-120121100253_1.html|access-date=2022-01-27}}</ref>

The company was awarded the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]]'s Defence Technology Absorption Award by Defence Minister [[Rajnath Singh]] in January 2021 for its work on the [[EMISAT]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Centum Electronics Limited Receives DRDO's Prestigious Defence Technology Absorption Award|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/business/business/centum-electronics-limited-receives-drdos-prestigious-defence-technology-absorption-award20210104183156/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=ANI News|language=en}}</ref> In March 2021, Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems CEO Rudra Jadeja stated that Centum Electronics was among the companies that contributed to the manufacture of [[Spice (bomb)|Spice 2000]] bombs including those used in the [[2019 Balakot airstrike]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bharadwaj|first=Swati|title=Spice bombs used in Balakot air strike were made in Hyderabad|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/spice-bombs-used-in-balakot-air-strike-were-made-in-hyd/articleshow/81538800.cms|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Times of India|date=17 March 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

Centum Electronics has been a partner of the non-profit [[Akshaya Patra Foundation]] since the 2000s. Between 2010 and 2020, Centum stated that it had sponsored meals for 360,000 school children at public and Government-aided schools in Bangalore.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-23|title=CSR: Centum Electronics sponsored meals for 3.6 lac school children over 10 years in Bangalore|url=https://thecsrjournal.in/csr-centum-electronics-sponsored-meals-for-3-6-lac-school-children-over-10-years-in-bangalore/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The CSR Journal|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Industry collaboration ==
An agreement has been signed by Nibe Space, a division of Nibe Defence and Aerospace on 9 September 2024, with Centum Electronics, [[Skyroot Aerospace]], [[AgniKul Cosmos]], SpaceFields, Sisir Radar, CYRAN AI Solutions, and [[Larsen & Toubro]] for the launch of India's first constellation of multi-sensor, all-weather, high-revisit [[Earth observation satellite|Earth observation satellites]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nibe Limited announces setting up India's first earth observation satellite constellation |url=https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/nibe-limited-announces-setting-up-indias-first-earth-observation-satellite-constellation20240908231908/ |access-date=2026-05-31 |website=ANI News |language=en}}</ref>

Centum Electronics Limited is an Indian electronics system design and manufacturing company. The company produces subsystems and microelectronics, and provides system integration services. The company was incorporated in January 1993 and is headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Centum has a presence in 6 countries. It has manufacturing facilities, design, and sales and support teams in India, Canada, and France, a design team in Belgium, and sales and support teams in the United Kingdom and the United States. The company's British subsidiary, Centum Electronics UK Ltd., services all European customers except those in France.  
Centum Electronics has multiple manufacturing facilities in Bangalore. The company opened its fourth Indian manufacturing facility at the Aerospace Park in Devanahalli, near Bangalore on 15 February 2017. Centum is one of the largest contractors to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and supplies over 50 different varieties of components for satellites and launch vehicles. Centum opened a new space facility in Yelahanka, Bangalore to support ISRO missions in September 2019.
